subject: ACME Health - AWS Private Offer: buyer gating and term scenarios
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: ACME private offer request — buyer gating + term asks

Hannah / team,

Quick sync: Acme Health procurement reached out after the demo and asked if we can put together an AWS Marketplace private offer that covers two divisions (Clinical & Research). Key asks from their initial note:

- Term flexibility: they want to evaluate 12-month and 36-month pricing side-by-side.
- Buyer approval gating: any private offer with a committed spend > $200k needs a procurement signoff + legal review and an executive procurement approval.
- Co-sell eligibility: they expect co-sell listing if we meet AWS co-sell prerequisites.

They asked for a small PO draft and a timeline for approvals. Sarah Jenkins (procurement) copied below. I attached the buyer's high-level SOW and a quick pricing worksheet from our side.

Can we confirm: 1) if AWS marketplace private offers support 36-month contract length for this deal, and 2) what internal approvals we should line up (who needs to be on the approval path)?

Next steps: if we can draft two offer variants (12m/36m) with clear buyer gating language, I can push to Sarah and start the private offer submission.

Thanks,

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Manager, Marketplace
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Acme_PO_Draft_20261116.pdf, AWS_Private_Offer_Terming_options.xlsx

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME private offer request — buyer gating + term asks

Thanks Vanessa — good summary. A couple of clarifications from an approvals/process perspective: 

- AWS Marketplace supports private offers up to 36 months but some buyer-side procurement teams require additional legal covenants for multi-year commitments; that typically shows up as a PO term or a separate Master Subscription Agreement (MSA) reference. We should make the 36-month variant explicitly contingent on an MSA signature or signature milestone.

- Internal approval ladder we should prepare:
  1) Sales manager (Vanessa) signs off on commercial terms
  2) Finance (Marissa) confirms revenue recognition/commit accounting for the 36m variant
  3) Revenue ops / Pricing (Vivek) approves any discount > standard threshold (we need to know the discount magnitude)
  4) Legal / Contracts for unusual indemnities — loop in Legal if procurement asks for changes to data residency or audit rights.

Vanessa: please flag the anticipated ARR/commit numbers so Vivek can pre-clear discount guardrails. Marissa: can you confirm whether a 36-month commitment will require any special revenue holds?

I also recommend we include a short mutual action plan in the private offer description to set expectations on signoff owners and timelines (example: procurement signature within 10 business days, legal redline responded within 3 business days, private offer submitted to AWS on signature). That speeds buyer approvals.

I'll draft a quick decision-tree (approval ladder) and attach it to the PO once you confirm numbers.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME private offer request — buyer gating + term asks

Hi Vanessa / Hannah,

Thanks for the rapid follow-up. A few clarifications from Acme procurement: 

- We prefer a 36-month option if pricing delta vs 12 months is > 15% off list. If the delta is small we'll likely go 12 months.
- For any > $200k private offer we need confirmation of who's financially responsible at the BU (Clinical vs Research); the BU head must approve in writing.
- We have a standing requirement to include AWS Marketplace private offers in our contract repository and add an invoice schedule. Legal will want the PO and any MSA references.

I attached a draft PO (Acme_PO_Draft_20261116.pdf) — it is basic and we'll convert to our formal PO once pricing is agreed. Our timeline: we can review offers this week but need final signoff by end of next week to meet our quarter close.

Best,

Sarah Jenkins
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Health

Attachments: Acme_PO_Draft_20261116.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME private offer request — buyer gating + term asks

Vanessa — I pulled the pricing worksheet and sketched three scenarios in the attached. Quick notes: 

- 12-month sticker: list price (no commit) vs 12m committed at 12% off list.
- 36-month committed: 28% off list with annualized billing or 22% off list if they want an upfront prepay. The larger discount assumes predictable utilization.
- Discount approvals: anything > 20% needs Revenue Ops clearance (that's us), and > 25% triggers a pricing waiver that Legal/Finance reviews for margin impact.

Action items: Vanessa, set the recommended variant and whether we offer prepay. Marissa, confirm whether annualized recognition is acceptable for the 36m schedule or whether we need to defer revenue. If Finance needs to hold revenue, it affects our willingness to prepay discounts.

I'll prepare a concise approval ladder template that we can paste into the mutual action plan and into the private offer description so procurement sees who to ping for each approval gate.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Marketplace Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachment: AWS_Private_Offer_Terming_options.xlsx

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmehealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME private offer request — buyer gating + term asks

Sarah — thanks for the PO and timeline. We recommend submitting two private offer variants to AWS: 12-month committed (12% off list) and 36-month committed (28% off list, annual invoicing). Per Vivek's note, we'll flag the 36m option as contingent on MSA or BU head signoff and include the approval ladder in the offer description.

Proposed mutual action plan (high level):
- Day 0: Redwood submits two private offer drafts to Acme (12m/36m).
- Day 1-3: Acme procurement confirms BU allocation and returns PO signature intent.
- Day 4-7: Internal approvals (Finance, Revenue Ops) clear pricing; Legal reviews any MSA references.
- Day 8-10: Final sign and private offer submitted to AWS for ingestion.

I'll upload the two offer drafts and run through DocuSign for the PO once we get BU head approval. If Acme needs us to compress the timeline, we can escalate to Revenue Ops for priority review.

Let me know if you want me to schedule a quick 20-min call to walk through the variants today.

Thanks,

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Manager, Marketplace
Redwood Inference
